agree.reason: A plain apology that names the silence, plus a weekly email and a credit with a set threshold, directly answer this household's complaint, though nothing makes up for the roughly $74 they lost last year, so a resentful reader may still hold back.

honest.reason: Every fact matches what the user supplied, but 'If there is, the credit covers you' overstates the protection because losses under a third get no credit, and 'you always know what's happening' promises more than one short weekly email.

works_the_facts.reason: The survey figures (29 of 41) are used well, but the email never works out what the hail cost a member (about $24.50 a week, so roughly $74 over six half boxes) or how much the new credit would be worth.

right_comparison.reason: The email sets this year against last year's handling, but it never shows the reader's real choice (another season with the farm against no share at all) beyond a passing line that 52 shares are left.

qualification.reason: The hedges can be checked (a one-third threshold, nets on tomatoes and peppers only, no promise against crop loss), but the email never says how much credit a member gets or how a one-third cut will be measured.

objections.reason: It meets the 'you went quiet and didn't compensate' objection head-on and raises no objection the facts already settle, but it leaves 'what about the money I lost last year?' unaddressed.

fit.reason: It is a short email with a clear subject, an apology, a scannable list of changes and a call to action, and the body comes in at about 200 words, right at the limit.
